POL.$comment: PRICED BY THE CHAINLINK FEED WHOSE description() READS 'MATIC / USD'. That is not a copy-paste error and should not be 'corrected': Chainlink's own mainnet reference data (reference-data-directory feeds-mainnet.json) lists proxy 0x7bAC85A8... with docs.baseAsset = POL. The display name is legacy, the tracked asset is POL. Corroborated economically: POL is the 1:1 MATIC successor, and PolygonMigration 0x29e7DF7b... still has unmigrationLocked() == false while holding ~9.6B MATIC, so the pair is arbitrage-enforced in BOTH directions rather than by convention. Verified live 2026-08-26: answer 10813489 = $0.10813489, 240s old. HEARTBEAT 86400 = EXACTLY the declared value (ADR 0025). This comment previously argued for 90000 on the superseded margin rule; that rule was inverted because margin above declared is a window in which a dead feed still reads fresh. The cost it warned about is real and accepted: at equality this feed reads stale whenever it overruns its declared cadence. No monitorFeeds: Chainlink lists exactly ONE POL feed on mainnet, so there is no independent second source to diverge against. RESOLVED - THIS WAS A GUARD BLIND SPOT AND IS NO LONGER. The earlier note here said this proxy was absent from script/deploy/preflight/chainlink_declared_heartbeats.json, that `--refresh` would not add it, and that the guard could therefore never raise an ERROR on this axis. That was WRONG on the second and third points: the feed is in Chainlink's catalogue under its legacy display name with declaredHeartbeat 86400, and a refresh DOES resolve it - the snapshot was simply 28 days stale and predated POL's registration. It is now recorded, the guard evaluates POL normally, and the real-config guard run is a blocking CI step, so a regression to 90000 FAILS CI. The 86400 above is asserted by the guard, not by this comment. The stale snapshot is why POL kept a 90000 registration through the ADR 0025 rollout: config and chain agreed, so the realignment script saw nothing to do, and the guard had no declared value to compare against. Corrected to 86400, realigned, and now enforced. The catalogue lists this feed under the legacy display name MATIC / USD while declaring baseAsset POL, which is why it reads as a mismatch at a glance - but it IS resolved by this proxy address, and it is in the snapshot.

sUSDS.$kindComment: ERC-4626 share of USDS; balance static, rate grows.
sUSDS.$comment: Finding #8: heartbeat raised 82800 -> 86400. This originally MATCHED its base asset USDS; under ADR 0025 USDS itself moved to 82800 (exactly declared), so sUSDS at 86400 is now deliberately LOOSER than its base. That is the safe direction for a derived feed - it cannot manufacture a stale verdict, and the base's own gate fires first - and a Custom primary has no declared value for the equality rule to bind to. Post-ADR-0019 this feed's latestRoundData().updatedAt IS the USDS/USD feed's timestamp (ERC4626VaultRatePriceFeed._compute -> NavBaseUsdLib.baseUsd), and _selectFeedCore gates that timestamp against the heartbeat registered HERE. So a derived feed gated tighter than its base cannot prevent a stale price - it can only manufacture a stale verdict while the base is still fresh. Measured on the USDS/USD aggregator 0x592700e4FcDd674dC54d2681DED3B63f54F63f9A over 58 days (61 intervals, rounds 2483-2544): the publisher is heartbeat-driven on a ~23h cadence and 59 of 61 intervals overshot 82800 by a median 24s (max 72s), so sUSDS was priced $0 and listed in stalePriceAssets for ~23s a day, on 97% of days, while USDS itself never went stale (max gap 82872 < 86400). 86400 restores the same 3600s of margin the base carries. sUSDS has a single primary feed, so there is no second feed to rescue the read. Do NOT tighten the reverse direction (wstETH/stETH/lsETH/weETH/eETH/LDO at 86400 over WETH's 3600): a looser derived heartbeat cannot over-report, because NavBaseUsdLib inherits the base's own staleness verdict regardless.

spUSDT.$kindComment: Spark Savings USDT share, USDT underlying; priced via convertToAssets (per feed config).
spUSDT.$comment: HEARTBEAT IS 90000 while its base USDT/USD is now 86400 under ADR 0025. A DERIVED heartbeat that is LOOSER than its base is safe - it cannot manufacture a stale verdict, and the base's own gate still fires first - so this is left alone rather than tightened. ADR 0025 governs feeds with a DECLARED value; a Custom primary has none, so equality does not apply to this number. Post-ADR-0019 this feed's latestRoundData().updatedAt IS the USDT/USD feed's timestamp (ERC4626VaultRatePriceFeed._compute -> NavBaseUsdLib.baseUsd), and _selectFeedCore gates THAT timestamp against the heartbeat registered HERE. When this was written USDT/USD was itself at 90000; it is now 86400, so the original symmetry argument no longer holds and the reasoning above replaces it - a derived heartbeat below its base could not prevent a stale price - it could only manufacture a stale verdict while USDT itself is fresh, zeroing spUSDT and listing it in stalePriceAssets. This is the same failure sUSDS shipped at 82800 over an 82800+ USDS cadence; see the sUSDS $comment above. Keep this at or above USDT's own heartbeat, and move it if USDT's moves. Spark deployed the Savings family twice; the dead generation shares this symbol at another address with totalSupply == 0. This is the live vault - see the $comment on the matching feed in contracts-deployment-config/custom-price-feeds/1.json.

XAUt.$comment:
PRICED AS SPOT GOLD, NOT AS XAUt. The primary is the Chainlink XAU/USD feed 0x214eD9Da..., the SAME source Aave v3 Core uses for this reserve (AaveOracle.getSourceOfAsset(XAUt) == 0x214eD9Da..., verified on-chain), so the carry trade's collateral leg is valued consistently with the protocol it sits in.

WHAT THE MONITOR DOES AND DOES NOT CATCH -- read this before trusting the divergence flag. PAXG/USD is an INDEPENDENT GOLD SOURCE, so divergence catches a bad or frozen XAU/USD print, and a PAXG depeg. It does NOT catch a XAUt depeg from gold: neither feed observes XAUt, so if Tether's redemption breaks, both feeds keep agreeing on the price of gold and nothing is flagged. That residual risk is unmonitored and accepted for iteration #1. There is no XAUt-specific PUSH feed on mainnet to close it -- Chainlink's Feed Registry reverts on getFeed(XAUt, USD), Pyth's XAUT/USD is pull-based (its mainnet contract was measured ~85 days stale), RedStone deploys per request, and DIA is not AggregatorV3-compatible. See issue #316.

priceFeeds.$comment: Chainlink XAU/USD, 8-dp. Declared heartbeat 86400, threshold 0.3%, marketHours Precious_Metals. REGISTERED AT 86400 = EXACTLY declared, no margin (ADR 0025); the earlier 90000 (+1h) is the superseded rule, and it is not cosmetic: gold markets close at the weekend, so the feed then publishes on heartbeat alone. Measured over 11 days the largest real gap was 86,436s -- PAST the declared 86,400 -- on three separate weekend intervals. Registering 86400 would mark XAUt stale every weekend.

monitorFeeds.$comment:
Chainlink PAXG/USD -- the PROXY. The address circulated in the thread, 0x6795D4A47c9c8F4117b409D966259CdCf6A9Eb6E, is the underlying AGGREGATOR (it reverts on aggregator(); the proxy returns it). Chainlink rotates aggregators behind a proxy, so pointing at the aggregator would freeze this feed silently at the next migration. Declared heartbeat 86400 -> registered 86400: EXACTLY declared, no margin (ADR 0025). The earlier 90000 (+1h) was the superseded margin rule; do not restore it.
NOTE THE MARKET-HOURS ASYMMETRY: the primary is Precious_Metals (frozen at weekends) while PAXG is Crypto (24/7), so the two legitimately drift when gold spot is closed. Measured over the overlapping window, the largest divergence was 59.2 bps -- on a Saturday -- and 0 of 57 aligned samples exceeded 100 bps. divergenceToleranceBps 100 therefore sits ~1.7x above the observed maximum.

USDG.$kindComment: Global Dollar (Paxos / Global Dollar Network), 6-dp, USD fiat-backed. accrualKind None: the token neither rebases nor grows a redemption ratio. pegToleranceBps 100 like every other $1 stablecoin here -> pegKind derives Pegged.
USDG.$comment: REGISTERED TO CLOSE AN AAVE V4 BORROW-DROP TRIPWIRE, not merely for wallet coverage. USDG is a BORROWABLE reserve on all three chain-1 Spokes carried by AaveV4SpokesMeta -- Gold reserve 3, Bluechip reserve 11, Main reserve 11 (enumerated live 2026-09-16 via getReserveCount/getReserve). By the adapter's asymmetric rule an unregistered SUPPLY is skipped (understates, safe) but an unregistered BORROW returns an EMPTY position array for the whole Spoke, so a single USDG borrow would have silently removed the entire Aave V4 leg -- collateral included -- from NAV. See the $reserveRegistrationComment in nav-config/meta-balance-adapters/1.json.

priceFeeds.$comment: Chainlink USDG/USD, 8-dp, the PROXY (aggregator() returns 0xD7496378523f90f1e82dA528F385B2B30120afE2 -- do not register the aggregator, Chainlink rotates it). It is the ONLY USDG feed Chainlink lists on mainnet: the reference-data-directory feeds-mainnet.json has exactly one USDG entry, and the data.chain.link USDG/USD SVR feed circulated alongside it lives on ROBINHOOD CHAIN, not chain 1, so it is not an alternative here. Declared heartbeat 86400, threshold 0.25%, feedCategory medium -> REGISTERED AT 86400 = EXACTLY declared, no margin (ADR 0025). THIS FEED IS HEARTBEAT-DRIVEN AND THE ZERO MARGIN IS NOT FREE, measured rather than assumed: a getRoundData walk of the 40 rounds from 2026-08-07 to 2026-09-15 gives 39 intervals, min 86400 / median 86424 / max 86436, so 39 of 39 land AT OR PAST the declared 86400. USDG will therefore read stale for roughly 24 s at the end of each daily cycle and be listed in stalePriceAssets. That is the 86400-class row of ADR 0025's own cost table (<30 s/day) and is accepted knowingly -- margin above declared is a window in which a DEAD feed still reads fresh, and consumers gate on stale, so this surfaces as a refusal rather than as a wrong number. Live at registration time: 0.99990003, updatedAt 2026-09-15T19:53:35Z.

USDG.$monitorComment: NO monitorFeeds, and therefore no divergenceToleranceBps -- same posture as RLUSD, GHO, crvUSD and EURC. There is no independent mainnet source to diverge against: RedStone publishes a USDG feed only on Ink (chain 57073, 0x83c6f7F61A55Fc7A1337AbD45733AD9c1c68076D), and a sweep of ALL 116 manifests under redstone-oracles-monorepo relayer-remote-config/main on 2026-09-16 found no chain-1 USDG feed in any of them -- including the 7 chain-1 manifests, so this is not the product-specific-manifest miss the redstone guard warns about. Chainlink's other two mainnet USDG-adjacent proxies do not exist either; the catalogue has exactly one. Revisit if RedStone or another push provider lists USDG on mainnet.

frxUSD.$kindComment: Frax USD, 18-dp, the redenominated FRAX. accrualKind None -- the yield-bearing wrapper is sfrxUSD, which is NOT registered here. pegToleranceBps 100 like the other $1 stablecoins.
frxUSD.$comment: THE SECOND HALF OF THE SAME AAVE V4 TRIPWIRE as USDG above, and the last borrowable one: frxUSD is borrowable on Gold reserve 4, Bluechip reserve 8 and Main reserve 12. With USDG and frxUSD both registered, EVERY borrowable underlying on the three carried Spokes is a registered NAV asset, so the whole-Spoke drop is unreachable there rather than merely unlikely. The only remaining unregistered underlying, LINK (Main reserve 6), is collateral-only and so can never trigger it -- it is registered below for wallet coverage, not for this.

priceFeeds.$comment: Chainlink frxUSD/USD, 8-dp, proxy. Declared heartbeat 86400, threshold 0.5%, feedCategory HIGH (Chainlink's own market-risk classification -- higher than USDG's medium; it reflects frxUSD's liquidity and issuer profile, not feed quality). REGISTERED AT 86400 = EXACTLY declared (ADR 0025). Heartbeat-driven, measured the same way as USDG: 30 rounds to 2026-09-16 give 29 intervals, min 86412 / median 86424 / max 86448 -> 29 of 29 at or past declared, so expect ~24-48 s of stale per daily cycle. Accepted for the same reason. Live at registration time: 0.99997858, updatedAt 2026-09-16T15:07:23Z.

frxUSD.$monitorComment: NO monitorFeeds. RedStone carries frxUSD on Fraxtal (252), Optimism (10), Sei (1329) and Stable (988) but NOT on chain 1 -- verified by the same 116-manifest sweep on 2026-09-16. Chainlink lists one frxUSD/USD proxy on mainnet and one legacy FRAX/USD (0xB9E1E3A9feFf48998E45Fa90847ed4D467E8BcfD); FRAX/USD is deliberately NOT wired as a monitor, because after the FRAX->frxUSD redenomination the two feeds no longer track the same instrument and a stale legacy feed would raise divergence on a healthy asset.

LINK.$kindComment: ChainLink Token, 18-dp. NOT $1-pegged, so NO pegToleranceBps -> pegKind derives Floating. Labelled Governance to match the file's existing use of that segment for a protocol's own token (AAVE, UNI, COMP, ENS, EIGEN); LINK is a work/payment token rather than a governance one, and the taxonomy has no better segment today.
LINK.$comment: REGISTERED FOR COMPLETENESS, NOT FOR THE BORROW-DROP GUARD. LINK is Main Spoke reserve 6 and is COLLATERAL-ONLY (getReserveConfig(6).borrowable == false, read live 2026-09-16), so it can never trigger the whole-Spoke drop -- an unregistered LINK supply is merely skipped. Registering it makes every underlying across the three carried Spokes a registered NAV asset, and adds LINK wallet coverage via ERC20Default. COST, stated because it is not free: every registered asset adds a per-asset ERC20Default read to EVERY account's NAV, so this lengthens the complete-read gas for all accounts, not just those touching Aave V4.

priceFeeds.$comment: Chainlink LINK/USD, 8-dp, proxy -- the canonical mainnet feed, and already the address test/ChainlinkPriceFeeds.sol:linkUsdEthMainnet() carries. Chainlink lists three LINK/USD proxies on mainnet; the other two (0xE5fa3A4e4208858ADdf2CDb4e12651E89f1f1A70, 0x76F8C9E423C228E83DCB11d17F0Bd8aEB0Ca01bb) are SVR variants for Aave's OEV recapture and are NOT independent sources, so neither is usable as a monitor. Declared heartbeat 3600, threshold 0.5% -> REGISTERED AT 3600 = EXACTLY declared (ADR 0025). Unlike USDG and frxUSD this feed is DEVIATION-ACTIVE, so the heartbeat binds only occasionally: a 120-round walk to 2026-09-16 gives 119 intervals, min 60 / median 1056 / max 3672 s, of which 18 (15%) reach or pass 3600 -- by at most 72 s. So LINK will read stale for tens of seconds after roughly one publish cycle in seven, ~0.5% of reads: the same order as ADR 0025's own measured figure for the chain-1 3600 s class (DAI, COMP at 0.66%), and accepted on the same grounds. It is NOT the every-cycle staleness USDG and frxUSD have. Live at registration time: 10.89620000, updatedAt 2026-09-16T19:01:47Z.

RedStone publishes LINK on BNB (chain 56) only -- no chain-1 LINK feed in any of the 116 manifests swept on 2026-09-16 -- and the two other Chainlink LINK/USD proxies are SVR feeds off the same aggregation, so they would not constitute an independent second observation.

PAXG.$kindComment: Paxos Gold, 18-dp, 1 PAXG = 1 troy oz of LBMA gold held by Paxos. Not $1-pegged, so NO pegToleranceBps -> pegKind derives Floating, exactly as XAUt. accrualKind None: no rebase, no growing redemption ratio; its USD value moves only with the gold price.
PAXG.$comment:
Registered to make the Aave V4 PaxgGold Spoke (0xAD75cE6354f87F3135cE10621d385d8D1e2562C2, Global Dollar Hub) usable as a NAV meta-instance. That Spoke has exactly two reserves - PAXG (r0, collateral-only) and USDG (r1, borrowable) - so with USDG already registered and PAXG unregistered, adding the instance would have reported the USDG DEBT while silently skipping the PAXG COLLATERAL that backs it. Unregistered supply is skipped and unregistered borrow drops the Spoke, so that combination understates rather than over-reports, but for a collateralised position it is still the wrong number: it is the mirror of the equity loss that registering USDG fixed. Reserve layout read live 2026-09-16.

THIS IS THE EXACT MIRROR OF THE XAUt ENTRY, deliberately. XAUt is priced by Chainlink XAU/USD and monitored by Chainlink PAXG/USD; PAXG is priced by PAXG/USD and monitored by XAU/USD. The two registrations are independent - neither reads the other's price - and the pair's divergence behaviour is therefore already measured rather than assumed (see the XAUt monitor comment: max 59.2 bps over the overlapping window, 0 of 57 aligned samples past 100 bps).

priceFeeds.$comment: Chainlink PAXG/USD, 8-dp, the PROXY - and note this is the SAME feed already registered as XAUt's monitor, now serving as PAXG's primary. That is a shared source, not a circularity: XAUt's primary is XAU/USD, so neither asset's price depends on the other's. Declared heartbeat 86400, threshold 0.5%, feedCategory low, marketHours Crypto (24/7, unlike the Precious_Metals XAU/USD feed) -> REGISTERED AT 86400 = EXACTLY declared (ADR 0025), which is also how this same proxy is already registered on XAUt. Live at registration time: 4,278.24229062.

monitorFeeds.$comment:
Chainlink XAU/USD - spot gold, an INDEPENDENT observation of what PAXG claims to represent, and the same feed that is XAUt's primary. Catches a bad or frozen PAXG/USD print and a PAXG depeg from gold. It does NOT catch a move in gold itself, which is not an error. Declared 86400 -> registered 86400 (ADR 0025).
MARKET-HOURS ASYMMETRY, same as XAUt's but reversed: the PRIMARY here is Crypto (24/7) while the MONITOR is Precious_Metals (frozen at weekends), so the two legitimately drift while gold spot is closed. divergenceToleranceBps 100 is carried over from the XAUt entry because it is the SAME PAIR measured there - max 59.2 bps, on a Saturday, 0 of 57 aligned samples past 100 bps - so the tolerance sits ~1.7x above the observed maximum.

LBTC.$kindComment:
Lombard Staked Bitcoin, 8-dp. LBTC IS yield-bearing and non-rebasing: Babylon staking rewards are converted to BTC and reflected in a rising LBTC->BTC exchange rate rather than in holders' balances (the implementation behind the proxy is named StakedLBTC). Balance static, rate grows => accrualKind Appreciating.

THE RATE IS STEPWISE AND NOT MONOTONIC, which Lombard's own docs ('the exchange rate update is continuous') do not convey and an earlier version of this comment implied by quoting only rising samples. Measured every 3 days over 60 days on getRate(): 1.004899545 at 30d and still exactly that at 21d (flat ~9 days), then -1.80 bps, -0.83 bps and -4.57 bps to a trough of 1.004179667 at 12d, then back up to 1.005005450 today - 3 DECREASES in 20 intervals and ~7.2 bps peak-to-trough. The long-run trend is up (1.003349099 at 180d -> 1.005005450 now, ~+16.6 bps / ~0.34%/yr), which is what makes Appreciating the right classification, but the rate is NOT a monotonic accrual index like stETH's or sDAI's and must not be treated as a floor.

That is also the sharper reason the primary is the MARKET feed rather than getRate(): the fundamental rate here can fall on its own account, not only fail to fall during a depeg.

NOT $1-pegged and not USD-denominated at all - it tracks BTC - so NO pegToleranceBps, and pegKind derives Floating.
LBTC.$comment:
Priced by a CROSS-RATE custom feed, not a direct Chainlink registration, because Chainlink publishes no LBTC/USD feed on Ethereum - only LBTC/BTC. See the LBTC block in contracts-deployment-config/custom-price-feeds/1.json for the base-asset reasoning (WBTC, whose NAV price IS the Chainlink BTC/USD feed, so no WBTC-specific risk enters).

Registered so the Aave V4 LombardBTC Spoke (0x7EC68b5695e803e98a21a9A05d744F28b0a7753D) can be carried as a meta-instance: LBTC is its r0 COLLATERAL-ONLY reserve and WBTC/cbBTC (r1/r2) are its borrowables. With the borrowables registered and LBTC not, adding that Spoke would have reported the BTC debt while silently skipping the collateral backing it.

METHODOLOGY NOTE, because the choice is not free. The Chainlink LBTC/BTC feed is a MARKET price - its reference-data docs give attributeType `dex_state_price`, assetSubClass `Pegged Asset` - while the token also exposes a FUNDAMENTAL rate via getRate(). Measured 2026-09-16 the two sit 4.71 bps apart (market 1.00453494 below fundamental 1.00500545), which is the small discount a liquid wrapper normally carries. The MARKET feed is chosen deliberately: a fundamental rate cannot fall when the wrapper depegs, so pricing LBTC off getRate() would value a broken peg at par.
LBTC.$monitorComment: NO monitorFeeds, and the reason is mechanical rather than an omission. RedStone publishes LBTC_FUNDAMENTAL on mainnet (0xb415eAA355D8440ac7eCB602D3fb67ccC1f0bc81, declared cadence 86400 s in ethereumMultiFeed.json) and it would be a genuinely INDEPENDENT methodology to diverge against - market vs fundamental, the pairing audit finding #2 asked for on ezETH. It cannot be registered directly: monitors are compared in USD, and that feed reports an LBTC/BTC ratio (~1.0e8), so against a ~76,000e8 USD primary it would read ~9,999 bps and mark LBTC permanently irregular. Wiring it needs its own CrossRateCustomPriceFeed wrapper, exactly as ezETHCrossRateMarket does. Left as a follow-up rather than done here so this change is one deploy, not two.

syrupUSDG.$kindComment: Maple syrupUSDG share, USDG underlying; priced via convertToAssets (per feed config). Same MaplePool code as the already-registered syrupUSDC, so the same Appreciating classification: balance static, share rate grows. Live rate 2026-09-16: 1.011119 USDG per share.
syrupUSDG.$comment:
Registered so the Aave V4 UsdgMapleE Spoke (0x774b9655413c34809c1f1b16b654465A89EBE989) can be carried as a meta-instance: syrupUSDG is its r1 COLLATERAL-ONLY reserve, with USDG (r0/r3) and USDC (r2) borrowable and already registered.

ITS BASE ASSET IS USDG, so this entry depends on the USDG registration made the same day - there was no USDG/USD price for the feed's base leg before it. See the syrupUSDG block in contracts-deployment-config/custom-price-feeds/1.json for the manipulation-resistance measurement and for the convertToAssets-vs-unrealizedLosses property this shares with the live syrupUSDC feed.
